Matrix Form of the Linear System (1).
From the definition of matrix multiplication we see that the $m$ equations of (1) may be written as a single vector equation
(2)
$$
\mathbf { A x } = \mathbf { b }
$$
where the coefficient matrix $\mathbf{A} = [a_{jk}]$ is the $m \times n$ matrix
$$
\mathbf{A}=\left[\begin{array}{cccc}a_{11} & a_{12} & \cdots & a_{1 n} \\ a_{21} & a_{22} & \cdots & a_{2 n} \\ \cdot & \cdot & \cdots & \cdot \\ a_{m 1} & a_{m 2} & \cdots & a_{m n}\end{array}\right], \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbf{x}=\left[\begin{array}{c}x_{1} \\ \cdot \\ \cdot \\ \cdot \\ x_{n}\end{array}\right] \quad \text{and} \quad \mathbf{b}=\left[\begin{array}{c}b_{1} \\ \vdots \\ b_{m}\end{array}\right]
$$
are column vectors.
